difficulty_reason: Counted unit is Lemma 6.12.8 at source lines 1989-1991: in the situation of the non-dependent recursion principle of Lemma 6.12.5, ap k (p-tilde'(b,y)) = p(b,y). The proof (source lines 1992-2021) is the last and most technical step of the flattening lemma and is not a computation: the pair path p-tilde'(b,y) has to be expanded into pairpath(p(b),q) using the canonical transport (line 1993), the auxiliary pair-path lemma must be instantiated at six named arguments (lines 1995-1999), its two factors then have to be computed separately, the first from the definition of the curried function d (lines 2003-2004) and the second from the induction computation rule for W passed across thm:dpath-arrow (lines 2005-2006), and the final identification is the observation that all paths in the resulting chain cancel in pairs (line 2020).
